title: inversedMixup: Data Augmentation via Inverting Mixed Embeddings

problem.claim: Existing augmentation approaches involve a tradeoff between the controllability of Mixup and the human interpretability of LLM-based generation.

gap.claim: A method is needed to bridge latent embedding space and discrete token space while retaining controllable mixing and producing interpretable text.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes inversedMixup, a unified framework combining Mixup's controllability with LLM-based generation's interpretability.

The framework aligns a task-specific model's output embedding space with an LLM's input embedding space so mixed embeddings can be reconstructed into human-interpretable sentences under a controllable mixing ratio.
The paper extends inversedMixup into a three-stage augmentation method and introduces a strategy to mitigate manifold intrusion during augmentation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating effectiveness and generalizability in few-shot and fully supervised scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Mixup augments samples by linearly interpolating inputs and labels with a controllable ratio.
Latent embedding-level Mixup produces samples that are not human-interpretable, while token-level LLM augmentation produces readable outputs with limited generation control.
inversedMixup bridges embedding and token spaces by aligning task-model output embeddings with LLM input embeddings for controllable sentence reconstruction.
The method is extended into a three-stage augmentation pipeline with a strategy to mitigate manifold intrusion.
The authors report effectiveness and generalizability across few-shot and fully supervised settings.

source_observation.claim: Aligning a task-specific model's output embedding space with an LLM's input embedding space enables mixed embeddings to be reconstructed as interpretable sentences.

interpretation.claim: A shared or aligned representation interface can combine controllable continuous-space operations with discrete-language generation.

application.claim: Use representation alignment when an augmentation workflow requires both tunable interpolation and readable generated examples.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the evaluated text augmentation settings.

source_observation.claim: The method identifies manifold intrusion in text Mixup and introduces a mitigation strategy.

interpretation.claim: Making augmented samples interpretable can expose failure modes that are difficult to observe in latent representations alone.

application.claim: Inspect reconstructed augmentation outputs to diagnose and mitigate intrusion or overlap phenomena.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how manifold intrusion is detected, measured, or mitigated.

unknowns: Datasets, tasks, model configurations, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
The implementation details of the three-stage augmentation method and manifold-intrusion mitigation strategy are not provided.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported effectiveness or generalizability.
